knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built by dividing annual costs and income by billable hours, so the work that can be billed recovers the costs. Using all paid hours, averages or wished-for rates does not do this.
The lesson says collection, inspection and return do not shrink with the size of the job, so a minimum charge covers the visit cost of a short job. It does not replace a written quote.

The lesson says to base the rate on the owner's own costs and billable hours, then compare it with verifiable local evidence. A single national average, a friend's rate or one bidding-site price is not enough.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract collection, admin, marketing, training, workshop upkeep and leave to find billable hours.
